newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AKZO NOBEL Q1 UP IN ALL UNITS BAR FIBRES.
newsitem.headline: AKZO NOBEL Q1 UP IN ALL UNITS BAR FIBRES.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Friday first-quarter profits rose 2.4 percent to 340 million guilders, supported by better results in all divisions except fibres and improved exchange rates.
"Pharma, Coating and Chemicals did better than last year, while Fibers reported lower earnings," the company said in a statement.
It added that generally higher currency exchange rates had also had a positive effect on earnings.
Akzo said the fall in operating income at its fibres unit reflected strong price pressure.
Operating profits at fibres more than halved to 18 million guilders from a year-earlier 45 million.

The chemicals group said operating profits at its high-margin pharmaceuticals group rose 15 million guilders to 198 million due mainly to the contribution of veterinary products maker Intervet and raw materials unit Diosynth.
In coatings, earnings at most business units were up year-on-year, reflecting higher volumes sold and recovered margins, Akzo said.
Operating profits at the division rose to 108 guilders from 81 million in the first 1996 quarter.
Akzo said higher earnings at chemicals mainly reflected improved results from its hydroprocessing catalyst activities, surface chemistry and polymer chemicals.
"The increase was partly offset by lower earnings of Base Chemicals as a result of scheduled maintenance stops," the company added.

A maintenance stop at Rovin and lower results from various chemicals firms also led to lower earnings from non-consolidated companies, which declined to 22 million guilders in the first 1997 quarter from 35 million a year earlier.
